title: 7.3.8 Lab: takeHit with a floor at zero
description: The enemy starts at 5 health and is hit for 2 at a time. Write `takeHit(n)` so that health comes off and never goes below zero — the rule lives in the class, not in the scene.

steps.title: Take the hit off this.hp
steps.instructions: Inside `takeHit(n)`, subtract the argument from `this.hp`. Run it and press Space: the number should count down 3, 1, and then keep going into negative numbers.
hints: Reread 7.3.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set). The subtraction is the same `this.hp -= n` shape.

steps.title: Stop at zero
steps.instructions: Now keep the result from going below 0. Write the guard *after* the subtraction: once the number has changed, pull it back up if it went too far. Press Space five times and check that the lowest number you ever see is `0`.
hints: An `if` that sets `this.hp` back to `0` when it has dropped below `0` is enough.
Write the guard after the subtraction, not before it: the guard has to look at the value that now exists.

requirements.title: takeHit(n) subtracts the argument from this.hp
requirements.description: The argument is taken off `this.hp` inside the method. Help: 7.3.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set)

requirements.title: takeHit(n) never leaves health below zero
requirements.description: After subtracting, the method brings `this.hp` back to `0` if it went negative (a guard `if`, or `Math.max`). Help: 7.3.6 (Worked Example: The number anyone can set)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "7.3.8 Lab: takeHit with a floor at zero". The task they were given: The enemy starts with 5 health and each Space press calls takeHit(2). Write the body of takeHit(n): take the argument off this.hp, then keep this.hp from going below zero, so the lowest number the enemy ever shows is 0. The rule lives in the class, not in the scene. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. moSHion facts that matter here: setup() runs once; draw() runs about 60 times a second, and so does every function it calls. kb.presses('space') is true only on the one frame a key goes down; kb.pressing('space') is true on every frame it is held. y grows downward. draw() shows this.hp as text on the enemy every frame. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable, parameter and helper-function names, template strings, arrow functions, a ternary or an if/else chain, x++ or x += 1 or x = x + 1, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Names that other code in the program already calls (takeHit) must keep those names, because a renamed one is never called. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, and the STEP comments the starter came with are not the student's work. The starter's takeHit is empty, which is missing on both criteria. Write each note for THIS student's own code, for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences, plain words. In a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: takeHit(n) subtracts the argument from this.hp
rubric.description: Inside takeHit, this.hp goes down by the parameter, whatever the student named it: this.hp -= n, this.hp = this.hp - n, or this.hp = Math.max(0, this.hp - n) all count. Subtracting a typed 2 instead of the parameter is not met: a hit of another size would be ignored.

rubric.title: takeHit(n) never leaves health below zero
rubric.description: When takeHit finishes, this.hp is never below 0: an if after the subtraction that sets it back to 0, a ternary, Math.max(0, ...) or max(0, ...), or an if/else that sets 0 when the hit is bigger than what is left. A check that only asks whether hp is above 0 BEFORE subtracting is not met: 1 - 2 still gives -1.
